claims.text: VBR can run custom scripts before the job starts and after it completes
VBR provides script settings for backup jobs to run scripts before and after the job
VBR provides pre-freeze/post-thaw scripts for application-aware processing
VBR runs custom pre-freeze/post-thaw scripts for VMs with non-VSS applications
For Linux VMs VBR runs custom scripts before and after snapshot creation to quiesce applications
EC2 guest scripting runs pre-snapshot/post-snapshot scripts to quiesce and restart applications
'Run scripts every backup session' option runs scripts before/after every policy session
Veeam Agent runs custom pre-job and post-job scripts within the backup job session
Veeam Agent for Windows uses pre-freeze/post-thaw scripts to quiesce the OS for non-VSS apps
VSPC: Veeam backup agent supports pre-freeze/post-thaw scripts
MABS runs pre-backup scripts before and post-backup scripts after a protection job
MABS runs scripts under the local system account and checks ScriptingConfig.xml on the protected computer

A.notes: Veeam and MABS covered (Veeam without the 10-minute timeout); silent on AWS and Cohesity, no enumeration line.

claims.text: Veeam Agent for Unix supports pre-job and post-job scripts, e.g. to quiesce an application
Veeam Agent for Linux supports pre-job/post-job scripts (agent computer and backup server in managed mode) plus pre-freeze/post-thaw scripts
Veeam Agent for Windows supports pre-freeze/post-thaw on the agent and pre-job/post-job on the backup server
VBR runs scripts on the backup server before/after the job via the Scripts tab in advanced settings
MABS supports pre-backup/post-backup scripts per data source in ScriptingConfig.xml on the protected computer
Pre-freeze/post-thaw scripts are for quiescence; advanced job-settings scripts relate to the job itself

B.notes: Veeam and MABS covered (no 10-minute timeout); silent on AWS and Cohesity.

claims.text: Microsoft 365 Backup is pay-as-you-go, consumption-based rather than seat-based
Backup Storage application tied to pay-as-you-go billing via a Billing Policy
Active Backup Storage Controller is responsible for billing in the Consuming Tenant
Charges based on user-facing OneDrive size in usage reports incl. first-stage recycle bin
Charges based on live mailbox size plus online archives
Cost breakdowns for OneDrive, Exchange and SharePoint
Departmental billing is supported
Usage reports exclude second-stage recycle bins and online archives, which must be calculated with PowerShell [5][6][7]
Get-MailboxStatistics can estimate online archive sizes
Veeam licensed per protected user account, one license unit each
All users with access to backed-up teams or non-personal SharePoint sites must be licensed
Subscription and Rental types; automatic update/usage reporting doubles allowed license overage
Rental license for service providers, term normally one month
Free Not For Resale license for demonstration and training

A.notes: Source [5] (and [6],[7] identical) only describes using usage reports and changing the period; it does not say second-stage recycle bins/archives are excluded. Missing the 31-day revocation and Teams/group-site exemption.

claims.text: Microsoft 365 Backup is pay-as-you-go, charged by consumption unlike user-based licenses
Billing set up via Azure subscription, resource group, region, owner/contributor role
Departmental billing segments costs into Azure subscriptions via multiple billing policies
Veeam licensed per protected user account, one unit each; restores need no license
Units consumed by mailboxes, OneDrive accounts and personal SharePoint sites backed up within last 31 days
Subscription license, 1-5 year term
Rental license, ~1 month, service providers only
Not For Resale free for demos/training; Evaluation free for testing
Community Edition: 10 users, 1 TB SharePoint, 10 teams

B.notes: Gold 3 credited: units consumed only by mailboxes/OneDrive/personal sites backed up in the last 31 days (implies revocation and that Teams/group sites do not consume).
